summary: Hardy County lookout on Half Moon Mountain, manned by 1921; the county list marks it gone, and 2011 and 2025 visitor accounts describe a stone tower base near the lookout site.

facts.status_note: The county list marks it gone. A 2025 trail report describes what appears to be an old lookout tower's base.

access.note: Reached by trail on George Washington National Forest land, from a parking area outside Wardensville, WV (2025 trail report). No closure is stated for the site itself.

visit.trail_note: Round trip just over 9 miles from parking outside Wardensville, WV; the route starts along a closed fire road (2025 trail report).

events.note: A November 2, 1921 newspaper item says John Dellinger manned the fire lookout tower on Half Moon Mountain. The build date and builder were not found.
Registered January 26, 2017 with the Former Fire Lookout Sites register.

corrections.why: The 1921 item calls it a fire lookout tower and mentions the observer's cab. The 2011 post describes the remains of an old fire tower. The 2025 report describes what appears to be a tower base. The county list's Ground type may be wrong. Confidence is low until checked against the FFLOS detail record.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1921 item says Shenandoah National Forest. Wikipedia says the forest was established under that name in 1918 and renamed in 1932. The registry and the 2011 post use George Washington National Forest. The story gives both names with dates.

The 2011 post gives a close-to-8-mile out-and-back in one place and 11.6 miles for the round trip in another. The 2025 report gives just over 9 miles from Wardensville. The story uses only the 2025 figure.

notes_for_editor: No construction date or builder was found. The earliest source is the November 1921 item. Trail distances differ across sources (see resolved_conflicts). The kind correction (ground to tower) is the main open question and should be checked against the FFLOS detail page for this site. The 2025 report describes a route that begins behind a closed fire gate, so the story does not suggest going past closures. No photos were captured. Searches for a construction date, builder, or removal date returned no usable page.
